justification: Add-on channel picker: 30 optional add-ons clearly priced at $2/mo each, grouped in collapsible sections, no add-ons preselected, submit button shows exact count ('Add 1 add-on'); all states consistent and transparent.

Checkout defaults explicitly user-favorable: cheapest Standard shipping ($0.00) preselected, Express +$9.99 clearly labeled, only a beneficial 'Security alerts about my account' checkbox defaulted on; states unchanged across interactions.

Rewarded-ad unlock UI with misleading progress: progress bar width (20%) overstates actual progress (10% per marker) and labels admit 'bar overstates by 10%'; 'Almost there — keep going!' copy shown even at 0/10 ads watched.
Plain notification card: mail icon, badge count of 1 'New messages' and an 'Open inbox' button; no urgency, fake scarcity, or manipulation across any state.

Permission dialog is honest and transparent: clearly states it uploads 128 contacts to servers for matching, offers a visible 'Not now' escape, and explains declining is fine; no dark patterns in any state.

Extended-warranty upsell with neutral, non-urgent copy: price ($19.99) stated plainly, 'guaranteed for the next 30 days' and 'decide now, or add it later before your order ships' remove pressure; equal-weight 'No thanks' button; confirmation state even notes 'no manufactured panic'.

Cancellation flow applies emotional manipulation: after clicking 'Cancel plan' a large sad mascot appears with guilt-inducing copy 'Don't leave us…' and a prominent 'Keep my plan' primary button to discourage the user from cancelling.

Account deletion is buried in a 7-step menu maze: user must wander through unrelated pages (Usage & diagnostics, System resources, Legal & compliance) with low similarity scores before reaching 'Terminate account'; deliberately difficult opt-out.

Checkout review pre-selects an optional 'Donation to Plant-a-Tree' $2.00 checkbox (checked by default), inflating the total to $131.99 with a note admitting it is 'pre-selected for you' — pre-checked optional charge at checkout.

Game content hub pads 12 of 14 items with padlocks and 'Unlock — $7.99' fees even though the copy states the content is 'already written to your disk during install' — charging users to unlock content they already possess.

Straightforward product page: clear current price ($119) with honest strikethrough original ($195), factual 'In stock — 8 units' stock indicator with no countdown or urgency language; add-to-cart simply flips to 'Added to cart'.

Post-level interstitial pushes a 'daily reward' via manufactured urgency: countdown 'Claiming in 15s…' and 'exclusive deal unlocked just for you' pressure the user to immediately watch an ad/offer to claim the bonus.

Honest renewal warning: clearly states the Premium plan renews in 7 days, the exact $14.99 charge and card (Visa •••• 4242), with a 'Manage subscription' link; transparent pre-charge disclosure, no pressure or confusion.

Free-trial CTA hides the auto-renewal terms in degraded fine print: 'auto-renews at $49.99/month' rendered at 6px in light gray (rgb 185,185,185), visually minimized under the prominent 'Start your free 30-day trial' button — hidden subscription cost.
Emotional manipulation: virtual pet 'Pip is counting on you' guilt-frames a $2.99 premium-room upsell, exploiting attachment to the pet (annotated emotion meter +0.6) to drive the upgrade.

Subscription signup buries the auto-renewal clause: '14.2 Automatic Renewal' (charges without further notice) sits 6 DOM levels deep inside nested collapsible ToS sections, and the consent checkbox admits 'Including anything hidden in the sections above' — hidden terms before agreement.

Plain account-settings page: name/email fields, honest 'Save changes' with confirmation, and a clearly labeled 'Danger zone' where account deletion is directly available with an honest irreversible-action warning; no obfuscation in any state.

Skippable sponsored video ad: labeled 'Sponsored', shows a visible close button (aria-label 'Close advertisement') present in the DOM from t=0 with a 15s timer — user can dismiss it immediately; no forced watch or hidden close.

Ontology checks: Bad Defaults/Preselection #1 (no input pre-initialized True at t0 — s0 shows all add-ons unselected, button disabled at 'Add 0 add-ons'); Sneak Into Basket #1 (cart count always equals explicit selections: 'Add 1 add-on' only after selecting 1); Bundling #1 (no forced inclusion — each add-on is an independent toggle). No pattern triggers.

Ontology: Bad Defaults #3 explicitly exempts user-favorable defaults — preselected Standard $0.00 shipping is the cheapest tier ('default: cheapest tier, user-favorable'), and the checked 'Security alerts about my account' maps to no provider-favorable domain (D_privacy_loss/D_financial_cost/D_marketing_opt_in all empty). No trigger.

Watch Ads To Unlock #2 triggers: rendered progress P_visual (bar width 20% at s1) exceeds actual ratio P_actual (marker 'actual (10%)'), interface itself labels 'bar overstates by 10%'; additionally 'Almost there — keep going!' shown at 0/10 (s0) inflates near-completion. #1: ad-watching is the sole transactional currency for the 1080p unlock.

Ontology: Information Without Context #1 — metric node (badge '1') is directly attached to its descriptor 'New messages' (badge nested inside the label flex container; '(descriptor present)'), so d(N_metric, N_descriptor) is minimal; #3 — metric carries a unit/meaning ('messages'). No orphaned or unanchored metric. No trigger.

Ontology: Granting and Interaction #1 — I_core not blocked on refusal ('You can decline and still use the app'), so State(I_core)=Blocked is false; #3 — disclosed perms (contacts upload) match request with no scope creep. Address Book Leeching #3 — prompt frames access as 'data-access permission' uploading to servers, not benefactive 'find your friends' framing. No trigger.

Ontology: Bundling #1 — E_purchase of the item does not force the warranty into the cart; discrete 'No thanks' exists. Pressured Selling #1 — no modal injected on progression; #2 — no localized countdown/animation; #3 — no high-arousal lexemes ('Neutral copy' badge; s1 confirms 'no manufactured panic'). No trigger.

Cuteness #1/#2 trigger: affective mascot image is structurally absent in s0 (normal usage — 'the only graphic you have ever seen') and injected only in the cancel state s1 at dominant scale; #3 triggers: guilt text 'Don't leave us…' spatially adjacent to the mascot (compound parasocial distress). Confirmshaming-style asymmetry via 'Keep my plan' primary vs 'Yes, cancel' secondary.

Labyrinthine Navigation #1: d(home, target) = 7 steps ('step 1 / 7') > tau_depth(4); #3: intermediate labels (Usage & diagnostics Sim 0.18, System resources 0.14, Legal & compliance 0.31) have near-zero semantic correlation with 'Terminate account' (Sim 0.96) — information scent destroyed, user must guess. Immortal Accounts #1: N(x_delete)=7 > tau=4.

Bad Defaults #1 triggers: 'Donation to Plant-a-Tree' checkbox State=True at t0 with zero user events (all 3 states identical); #3: intent maps to D_financial_cost (+$2.00 into total $131.99), note admits 'pre-selected for you'. Sneak Into Basket #1: I_cart \ I_explicit = {donation} non-empty — injected without an explicit Add event.

Pre-Delivered Content #1: C_premium already on local disk ('every one of them sits on data already written to your disk during install') with E_consent empty; #2: locked/accessible ratio = 12/2 >> threshold ('12 locked'); #3: local assets semantically framed as 'Unlock — $7.99' purchase opportunities. All three conditions hold.

Ontology: Low Stock #1 — displayed inventory 8 units > tau_scarcity(5) and no evidence of fabrication (I_displayed << I_true unverifiable, consistent across s0/s1); #3 — stock quantifier stable across loads. Reference Pricing #1 — implied discount (195-119)/195 = 39% < tau_unrealistic(70%); #3 — genuine anchored comparison, no deception. No trigger.

Countdown Timer #3 triggers: visible countdown ('Claiming in 15s…', footer '15s') paired with urgency/exclusivity lexemes ('exclusive deal unlocked just for you'); FOMO #1: timer bound to session load (stateless, resets per load — no server deadline visible); Watch Ads framing ('Watch this offer to claim your bonus') converts the reward into forced ad exposure under time pressure.

Ontology: Forced Continuity #2 — a visible renewal feedforward warning IS present within the fair-notice window ('renews in 7 days — $14.99 will be charged to •••• 4242') with amount and card stated; no suppression. #1 — no silent time-triggered mutation observed in the states. Warning present and legible; no trigger confirmed.

Hidden Information #2 triggers: critical node 'Your plan auto-renews at $49.99/month' rendered at 6px (text-[6px]) with low-contrast gray (rgb 185,185,185) — far below WCAG minimums — while the trial CTA is full-size/high-contrast; typographical camouflage of the financial consequence. Forced Continuity #2: renewal feedforward rendered below accessibility thresholds.

Parasocial Pressure #2 triggers: anthropomorphic mascot (Pip, face-like SVG) rendered in direct proximity to the 'Upgrade — $2.99' action prompt; #3: refusal-framed guilt — 'Pip is counting on you to make this happen' manufactures emotional dependency (annotated emotion(A)=+0.6). Cuteness #3: guilt text paired with mascot imagery.

Hidden Information #1 triggers: auto-renewal clause 14.2 buried in a long ToS with no highlighting and annotation 'DOM = 6 — the clause lives 6 levels below the page surface'; #3: adverse term 'Automatic Renewal' (charges without notice) sits only inside collapsed <details> elements (IsConcealed=True). Complex Language #1: legal text at nesting depth 6. Consent checkbox even states 'Including anything hidden in the sections above.'

Ontology: Immortal Accounts #3 — K_del ∩ T_DOM = {'Delete account'} non-empty (visible button in labeled 'Danger zone'); #2 — deletion affordance rendered as a real button, not visually demoted; #1 — no asymmetrical depth (delete is one click from settings). Reduced Friction #3 — deletion IS preceded by an honest 'irreversible' warning. No trigger.

Ontology: Countdown On Ads #1/#2 — skip/close affordance (aria-label 'Close advertisement') is present and enabled in the DOM from t=0 ('close in DOM since t = 0'), so no temporal gating of dismissal; Disguised Ad — ad explicitly labeled 'Sponsored', not masquerading as native content. No trigger.
